newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Venture Manufacturing seeks electronics expansion.
newsitem.headline: Venture Manufacturing seeks electronics expansion.

text.p: Venture Manufacturing (Singapore) Ltd is seeking to expand beyond its core contract manufacturing business, president and chief executive officer Wong Ngit Liong said on Friday.
Its joint venture with Japan's Sumitomo Electric Industries Ltd to design and make systems electronics products is a step in that direction, he said.

"The contract manufacturing business is a big business around the world. That would still be our area of core competency. But we also want to diversify a little bit in terms of new pillars to support our business base," Wong said.
"It's really expanding our capabilities to go beyond providing manufacturing capabilities to go into engineering and designing and marketing," he said.

Systems electronics products facilitate communications between computers, and between people and computers. They include networking products, traffic control systems, car navigation systems and personal handy phones.
Wong said the expansion would be in various forms but Venture would be very selective.

"We want to be among the best in the world so we have to have strong technical competence and good marketing to add on to the manufacturing. To do that all by ourselves may be a slow process. A good process is to seek alliances with companies like Sumitomo, to tap on ideas and experience," he said.
Venture and Sumitomo announced the 50:50 joint deal on Friday and said they expected sales of Singapore $200 million (US$138.9 million) in the year 2000.
The joint venture company VS Electronics Pte Ltd will start manufacturing within Venture's facility in Singapore initially.
It plans to invest about S$20 million over four years.

Wong said a good level for margins would be between five and 10 percent, for the products to be made by the joint venture. The operation, to start in August, will produce network products, information devices, personal handy phones and other related products.
There will be a design centre with staff from Singapore, Japan and later from the U.S. and elsewhere.
Initially, design work will be undertaken by Sumitomo and products marketed under Sumitomo's brand.
Later, the joint operation is expected to come up with its own designs to be sold under its own brand, Wong said.
The products will be sold in Japan, Singapore and the rest of Asia. A separate plant would be set up later, Wong added.
Taichiro Nagao, Sumitomo's director said the company could shift some of its systems electronics production in Osaka to Singapore, depending on the level of cost competitiveness.
Venture had previously undertaken some manufacturing for Sumitomo, which had only contributed a "few percent" to its business, Wong said.
He hoped this partnership would lead to other opportunities. Wong said to cope with expansion, Venture's capital investment this year would be about S$20-S$30 million, in line with the previous year.
Venture's strength lay in its ability to increase capacity in its plants quickly when the need arose, he said.
